nodes.label: clean_description() HTML cleaning
nodes.rationale: Strips page-builder scaffolding (Magento PageBuilder, Avada/Fusion Builder, wrapper divs, <style>), keeps headings/lists/paragraphs. Default is cleaned HTML; the sample keeps raw markup. Open question for the client: cleaned vs raw.

nodes.label: Option1/2 value resolution
nodes.rationale: Woo option values come from parent attributes[].terms joined to variations by id; fallback = variation label string; fallback = synthesised grid. Option1 Name = Colour for multi-colour products, Title for single-variant; single-variant Option1 Value = Default Title.

nodes.label: Matrixify multi-row product model
nodes.rationale: Row 1 carries product-level fields + variant 1 + image 1; one row per further variant; trailing rows carry only Handle + Image Src + Image Position for gallery overflow. Product-level fields appear only on the first row.

nodes.label: ScraperAPI unblocker
nodes.rationale: Tested end to end: clean pages, real product data, 1 credit per request. One full crawl ~= 1,542 credits; project with dev re-runs ~6-10k, run on one month of the Hobby plan (USD $49 / 100k credits), cancelled on delivery. Removes Akamai as a project risk.

nodes.label: Oakley size-variant explosion
nodes.rationale: Parser handles eyewear (one-size) today. ~580 products (apparel 310, footwear 35, goggles) need the size axis parsed from the PDP and exploded colour x size; ~8-10 hrs.

nodes.label: Oakley crawl circuit breaker
nodes.rationale: After 3 Akamai-blocked requests in a row it aborts in ~30s and keeps what was scraped, replacing 20+ min of exponential backoff. A run that scrapes 0 products is not written so the last good CSV survives.

nodes.label: Cloudflare R2 image bucket
nodes.rationale: S3-compatible (boto3), key oakleysi/<handle>/<NN>.jpg, public r2.dev URL. Free tier (10 GB storage, 1M writes/mo) covers the ~1-2 GB / ~14k-file catalogue at $0. Equivalents: Backblaze B2, AWS S3, DigitalOcean Spaces with the same boto3 code.

nodes.label: CurlCffiFetcher (fetch.py)
nodes.rationale: curl_cffi impersonates Chrome TLS/JA3, throttles 3s + jitter, detects the challenge stub via expect= (page missing /en-us/product/ or pdp-hero-name) and backs off exponentially. make_fetcher() routes through ScraperAPI or a proxy when .env provides one. fetch.py is the swap point for a browser fallback.

nodes.label: Matrixify-style Shopify import sheet
nodes.rationale: Output mirrors vertx_product_submission_sample.csv: one row per variant, product fields on the first row, gallery rows after. Import with Matrixify, not the native Shopify importer; everything imports as draft with a blank price.

nodes.label: Oakley image re-hosting pipeline (Option A)
nodes.rationale: Scrape-only engagement means images cannot go into the client's Shopify Files, so delivered CSV Image Src URLs point at a bucket we host for the import window then tear down. Download origin PNG -> flatten to white JPEG, cap ~1600px q~85 -> upload to Cloudflare R2 -> rewrite Image Src / Variant Image to the public bucket URLs.

nodes.label: Oakley PDP parser
nodes.rationale: PDPs are server-side rendered: title, breadcrumb -> Type, cleaned description + measurements, SEO description, image gallery, per-colour Sku/UPC. Apparel/footwear/goggle size explosion and colourway grouping are stubbed (eyewear is one-size).

nodes.label: Oakley sitemap.xml product discovery
nodes.rationale: /en-us/sitemap.xml returns all 1,541 product URLs in one request with <lastmod> for incremental runs; falls back to the category crawl if the sitemap is unavailable.

nodes.label: utag_data.Products variant block
nodes.rationale: Each Oakley PDP embeds utag_data.Products = {<UPC>: {Sku, FrameColor, LensColor, LensTechnology, LensType, Category, ModelName, ...}} giving per-variant barcodes and attributes with no login. Parsed with a brace-matcher because it is a JS object literal with unquoted numeric keys, not JSON.

nodes.label: Shopify Submission Format column map
nodes.rationale: Source of truth is vertx_product_submission_sample.csv, a Matrixify (Excelify) sheet, not a native Shopify CSV. Column order does not matter to Matrixify, names do; unused columns can be omitted. The header row is reproduced verbatim from the sample.

nodes.label: Client-facing quote (for Howard)
nodes.rationale: Fixed AUD $2,000 for all three brands plus ~$75 at-cost scraping-proxy subscription; ~3 week timeline; phased alternative ($350 / $900 / $750). Poses 7 confirmation questions incl. Crispi scope, description style, Oakley colourway grouping, pricing, reseller authorisation, and image hosting option A/B/C.

nodes.label: Internal working quote (rev 2)
nodes.rationale: ~32 hrs done + ~57 left ~= ~90 hrs at AUD $22/hr ~= $2,000 labour + ~$75 infra. The three timeline risks (Akamai, image hosting, product discovery) are done and proven in a live Shopify import; what remains is catalogue-scale build and QA. Lists 16 risks/assumptions.

nodes.label: Oakley SI Holbrook PDP fixture

nodes.label: Oakley colourway grouping decision
nodes.rationale: Oakley lists each colour of a model as its own product page. Default = mirror the source (one Shopify product per colourway). Grouping into one product with a Colour option adds ~4-10 hrs on Oakley; needs a client decision.

nodes.label: Crispi AU = 13 products scope
nodes.rationale: The brief's 'Cirspi / cirspiaustralia.com.au' does not resolve; the live site is crispiaustralia.com.au. 13 products is the entire AU catalogue (verified via store API + category counts). Crispi globally makes 40+ models on crispi.com, a different site and re-scope. Confirm with the client.

nodes.label: The Akamai wall
nodes.rationale: Oakley SI is behind Akamai Bot Manager. requests/WebFetch get 403; curl_cffi with Chrome JA3 impersonation works for ~40-50 requests then serves a JS-challenge stub; only a real/stealth browser sustains access but is 3-8s/page. Strategy: fast path (curl_cffi, optionally browser-seeded cookies) for bulk, browser only where challenged; get past a full run via ScraperAPI unblocker or a rotating residential proxy set in .env, or seed _abck/bm_sv cookies from a real browser.

nodes.label: Oakley AVIF media-processing failure
nodes.rationale: assets*.oakley.com does Accept-header negotiation and serves AVIF, which Shopify rejects. Query params force origin PNG but do not survive Shopify's CSV importer; browser downloads give AVIF-with-a-.png-name. Verified fix: origin PNG -> flatten to white JPEG -> serve from our own bucket.

nodes.label: Crispi Option1-first packing fix (_resolve_options)
nodes.rationale: Crispi imported '0 products added' because size-only products had Option2 Name set with Option1 Name empty, which Shopify silently rejects. Fixed: options now pack into Option1 first, so a size-only boot is Option1 Name = Size; also dropped the sample's stray trailing space in 'Size '.

nodes.label: --fast mode (1 request/product)
nodes.rationale: Skips per-colour page fetches so ~3x more products scrape before the Akamai block. Every colour still gets its barcode (on the main page) but colours 2+ get a generic label and no per-colour SKU. Testing lever only; the deliverable run uses full mode + proxies.

nodes.label: WooCommerce variation SKU gap
nodes.rationale: Both Woo sites' Store API under-reports variations (Crispi returns 0-1 of ~12 sizes). The scraper synthesises the full option grid so structure is right, but synthesised rows have no SKU. Fix = parse each product page's variation form (data-product_variations / ?wc-ajax=get_variation), costed in the finish hours.
